---
title: "Installing METIS"
---

METIS is a Python package. We use [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to install it
and manage the dependencies in your own project.

## Installation

1. Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and
   [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads).

2. Create a project for your surrogate work:

   ```bash
   uv init my-surrogate --python 3.13
   cd my-surrogate
   ```

3. Choose a PyTorch build. For CPU training on **Linux or Windows**:

   ```bash
   uv add "torch>=2.10,<3" --index pytorch-cpu=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
   ```

   In `pyproject.toml`, add `explicit = true` to the index entry so only PyTorch
   uses this index:

   ```toml
   [[tool.uv.index]]
   name = "pytorch-cpu"
   url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
   explicit = true
   ```

   On **Apple Silicon macOS**, use `uv add "torch>=2.10,<3"` instead. The current
   PyTorch range does not support Intel Macs.

4. Install METIS with the dependencies used in these tutorials:

   ```bash
   uv add "metis-surrogate[docs] @ git+https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git"
   ```

5. Check the installation with a short fit on the bundled SIRDS data:

   ```bash
   uv run metis demo --steps 100 --output metis-demo
   ```

   This saves a surrogate, metrics and predictions in `metis-demo/`.

Run your scripts with `uv run python your_script.py`. uv manages the environment
in `.venv`; there is no need to activate it manually. Keep `pyproject.toml` and
`uv.lock` with your project so the environment can be recreated.

::: {.callout-note}
The distribution is **metis-surrogate**, imported in Python as **metis**. It is
not yet on PyPI; the PyPI package named `metis` is unrelated. Python 3.11+ is
supported. `[docs]` includes notebook and plotting dependencies; for a smaller
installation, use `[plots]` or omit the extra entirely. Add `[wandb]` when using
Weights & Biases.
:::

## Running the tutorial notebooks

Each worked example shows its executed outputs. Under **Other Formats**, choose
**Jupyter** to download it. To run downloaded notebooks in your project:

```bash
uv add --dev jupyterlab
uv run jupyter lab
```

Open the notebook in JupyterLab and choose **Run all**. If using another notebook
editor, select your project's `.venv` Python kernel.

Alternatively, choose **Open in Colab**, then **Runtime → Run all**. A shared
setup cell installs the matching METIS revision and dependencies using uv;
you do not need to write installation commands. The examples run on CPU.
Colab runtimes are temporary, so a new runtime needs setup again. If setup asks
for a session restart because a library was already loaded, restart once and
run all cells again.

## Optional CUDA setup

For an NVIDIA GPU, select a compatible build using the
[uv PyTorch guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/pytorch/).
For example, for CUDA 12.8:

```bash
uv add "torch>=2.10,<3" --index pytorch-cu128=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
```

Set `explicit = true` on this index as above, then check the installation:

```bash
uv run python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())"
```

Use `TrainingConfig(device="cuda")` in Python, or
`uv run metis train training.device=cuda` with Hydra. The PyTorch installation
does not install or update your NVIDIA driver.

::: {.callout-tip}
To develop METIS itself, follow the [contributor guide](https://github.com/OJWatson/metis/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for cloning the repository, running tests and building the documentation.
:::
